evidence.text: Subtract a specified matter history from the measured or modeled expansion rate and logarithmically differentiate the residual.

sources.title: On the Cosmological Implications of the String Swampland

evidence.text: Linearize the constant-c flow in c while retaining matter-to-dark-energy evolution of Ωφ, then select the solution regular as Ωφ → 0. This reconstruction reproduces the analytical expression supplied for the limiting orbit.

sources.title: Warm DBI inflation with constant sound speed

evidence.text: Specify H(φ), reconstruct the DBI velocity and sound speed, calculate logarithmic derivatives, and integrate the remaining e-folds. A potential supplies H approximately when its energy dominates.

sources.title: The Swampland, Quintessence and the Vacuum Energy

evidence.text: Compare the loop-potential change across a scalar interval with the allowed dark-energy density. Estimate coupling derivatives using loop-factor counting and distinguish absolute from relative changes.

sources.title: Model independent analysis of supernova data, dark energy, trans-Planckian censorship and the swampland

evidence.text: Allow field-dependent dark-matter masses, determine the resulting energy exchange, and rewrite the dark-energy continuity equation using an effective equation of state. Transfer must exceed a model-dependent threshold to yield w_eff<-1.

sources.title: Consistency of Cubic Galileon Cosmology: Model-Independent Bounds from Background Expansion and Perturbative Analyses

evidence.text: Integrate the scale-independent growing-mode equation using H, Ωm and Geff/G, then differentiate lnD+ and form ln f/lnΩm. This operation separates actual model growth from an approximate γ inferred only from the background.

sources.title: Revisiting Scalar Tensor inflation by swampland criteria and Reheating

evidence.text: Can a scalar-dependent gravitational coupling accommodate slow-roll inflation, the observed scalar/tensor spectra, and the paper's swampland cuts? The study also asks which effective reheating equations of state give positive, relatively short expansion histories.

sources.title: Swampland conjecture in $f(R)$ gravity by the Noether Symmetry Approach

evidence.text: Can symmetry-selected f(R) gravity connect a conjectural quantum-gravity origin with primordial and present cosmic acceleration? The paper investigates scale-factor duality together with bounds on an effective scalar potential.

sources.title: Scalar speed limits and cosmology: Acceleration from D-cceleration

evidence.text: How do quantum higher-derivative effects constrain motion toward an enhanced-symmetry point on scalar moduli space, and can the resulting slowing mechanism generate accelerated cosmology without a flat scalar potential?

sources.title: Anisotropic dark energy from string compactifications

evidence.text: Can a string-inspired modulus–axion system coupled to a pure U(1) vector produce stable late-time acceleration with small anisotropy despite a steep scalar potential, and are the required couplings compatible with the compactification structures considered?

sources.title: Holographic origin of TCC and the distance conjecture

evidence.text: What asymptotic information can weakly coupled particles retain in a universe driven by a scalar rolling down a positive exponential potential?

sources.title: Trans-Planckian Censorship and the Swampland

evidence.text: What quantum uncertainty applies to the scalar assigned to an entire Hubble patch? Appendix C treats that scalar as a normalized spatial average on a Cauchy surface, with RMS field displacement and RMS velocity.

sources.title: Late-time attractors and cosmic acceleration

evidence.text: When are scaling cosmologies inevitable late-time attractors of multi-field multi-exponential potentials, and how do exponential couplings constrain cosmic acceleration without assuming slow roll?

sources.title: The String Theory Swampland in the Euclid, Square Kilometer Array, and Vera Rubin Observatory Era

evidence.text: Can a canonical scalar dominate sufficiently late and generate negative enough pressure for acceleration while satisfying potential restrictions? The calculation assumes flat cosmology and approximately Ωφ,0=0.7.

sources.title: Revisiting the scalar weak gravity conjecture

evidence.text: Can the constrained scalar potentials drive late-time acceleration? The paper compares their logarithmic slopes with an imported canonical scalar-dominated fixed-point condition.

sources.title: Limits from Weak Gravity Conjecture on Dark Energy Models

evidence.text: A decaying vacuum with physical EoS −1 cannot be separately conserved. The model supplies an interaction with dust and asks whether an effective canonical scalar description can satisfy the excursion criterion.

sources.title: Cosmology of light towers and swampland constraints

evidence.text: Can cosmological evolution and EFT consistency constrain how rapidly light-tower masses and positive runaway potentials decay at asymptotic field distance, particularly by providing upper bounds on their exponential rates?

sources.title: Swampland conjecture in $f(R)$ gravity by the Noether Symmetry Approach

evidence.text: How do power-law curvature corrections affect scalar criteria and cosmological behavior? The paper treats epsilon as a theory parameter and separately expands near the General Relativity value epsilon=0.

sources.title: The zoo plot meets the swampland: mutual (in)consistency of single-field inflation, string conjectures, and cosmological data

evidence.text: How does a nearly flat canonical scalar potential generate approximately constant expansion, and which dimensionless derivatives control this approximation?

sources.title: Accelerating cosmology from Λ < 0 gravitational effective field theory

evidence.text: Can negative-Λ gravitational EFTs support observationally plausible accelerated expansion while retaining time-symmetric bang/crunch solutions with asymptotically AdS Euclidean continuations, and can the required scalar potentials arise from a superpotential?

destination.title: Origins and composition of dark energy
destination.question: Which matter, field, thermal or geometric mechanisms could account for apparent dark energy and its relationship to dark matter?
destination.summary: Organizes competing mechanisms without identifying their degrees of freedom or effective descriptions.

systems: Unified, brane-derived, thermal and geometric dark sectors
targets: Simultaneous or coordinated dark-matter and dark-energy behavior
regimes: Late-time cosmology, with source-specific earlier histories
assumptions: Mechanisms are alternatives, not a shared physical model.
conventions: Simultaneous clustered matter and smooth dark energy differs from successive matter-like and dark-energy-like phases.
excludes: Established viability of every proposed mechanism

sources.title: Dark Energy from Structure: A Status Report

evidence.text: Can the effects assigned to Dark Energy arise from averaging ordinary inhomogeneous matter and geometry in Einstein gravity? The question includes whether an FLRW prior changes the interpretation of observations taken on different scales and at different epochs.

sources.title: Dark Energy from Structure: A Status Report

evidence.text: Does an inhomogeneous universe evolve on average like an FLRW solution, and can structure-induced backreaction explain apparent Dark Energy within classical general relativity? This status report reviews the mechanism and strategies for establishing its quantitative and observational relevance.

sources.title: New Scalar Field Quartessence

evidence.text: The cosmological evolution is described through interacting vacuum and matter components, a canonical scalar representation, and an axion–condensate system. Comparing these descriptions requires separate field and energy-component dictionaries.

evidence.text: Can the collective thermal behavior of a sector slightly displaced from a conformal fixed point generate late-time dark energy through a limiting temperature, while behaving like radiation early enough to satisfy cosmological constraints?

sources.title: Dark Energy from Structure: A Status Report

evidence.text: Riemannian volume averaging of scalars: ⟨Ψ⟩D=VD⁻¹∫D ΨJ d³X. The commutator ∂t⟨Ψ⟩D−⟨∂tΨ⟩D=⟨ΘΨ⟩D−⟨Θ⟩D⟨Ψ⟩D exposes correlations between local expansion and the averaged field without requiring perturbation theory.

sources.title: New Scalar Field Quartessence

evidence.text: Background evolution after release is approximated by ϕ̈0+3Hϕ̇0=V0 exp(−ϕ0/f)/f. The discussion imports fixed-point results for exponential potentials with a perfect fluid and separately estimates whether thermal freeze-out could supply the required particle abundance.

sources.title: String-Inspired Running Vacuum—The “Vacuumon”—And the Swampland Criteria

evidence.text: Integrate the kinetic identity along H(a), then eliminate a from U(a). The output preserves the input equation-of-state dependence and matches background total stress-energy.

sources.title: Emergent dark energy from unparticles

evidence.text: Use a near-conformal trace anomaly and imported thermal-average expressions for energy density and pressure. Solve the unparticle continuity equation to obtain a(y), then combine it with the Friedmann equations and early- and late-temperature expansions.

sources.title: Dark Energy from Structure: A Status Report

evidence.text: Closure strategies include prescribed effective equations of state, coupled power-law solutions for backreaction and curvature, and relativistic Lagrangian approximations using Cartan coframes. One proposed construction models QD perturbatively, then evolves the averaged model through the exact scalar framework.

sources.title: Dark Energy from Structure: A Status Report

evidence.text: Actively smooth a spatial metric with a mass-preserving Ricci flow, then compare averaged quantities on the original and fitting geometries. This addresses geometric fitting in addition to averaging scalar evolution.

sources.title: Perspectives on the Dark Sector

evidence.text: What limitations does point-particle EFT face in explaining dark energy and primordial structure, and what prospects do a heterotic unified dark sector and high-temperature matrix-model emergent cosmology offer?

sources.title: Limits from Weak Gravity Conjecture on Dark Energy Models

evidence.text: The scalar excursion depends on how the dark component shares the expansion rate with independently specified matter. Distinguishing baryon-only matter from a separate dark-matter component is essential when a Chaplygin fluid may itself unify dark matter and dark energy.

sources.title: Limits from Weak Gravity Conjecture on Dark Energy Models

evidence.text: Can tachyon or generalized Born–Infeld descriptions evade the difficulty found for canonical Chaplygin reconstructions? The paper explicitly leaves this question open and supplies no corresponding quantum-gravity bound or noncanonical calculation.

sources.title: Possible Theoretical limits on holographic quintessence from weak gravity conjecture

evidence.text: The background specifies how the matter fraction and holographic dark energy determine cosmic expansion before converting the dark-energy fluid into a scalar trajectory.

sources.title: Dark Energy: A Brief Review

evidence.text: What could explain a small, nonzero dark-energy density and its present comparability to matter, and how can expansion and structure-growth observations distinguish proposed explanations?

sources.title: Building Supergravity Quintessence Model

evidence.text: The model-building target is dynamical dark energy in supergravity. A viable scalar must avoid a gravitino-scale mass, retain sufficiently slow evolution at the present Hubble scale, and couple weakly enough to ordinary matter to pass gravitational tests.

sources.title: A Dynamical solution to the problem of a small cosmological constant and late time cosmic acceleration

evidence.text: Can nonlinear kinetic scalar dynamics explain why negative-pressure dark energy becomes important only recently, by linking its evolution to matter–radiation equality rather than tuning an initially tiny dark-energy density?

sources.title: Dark D-brane Cosmology

evidence.text: Can a moving hidden-sector D-brane supply interacting dark matter and DBI dark energy with geometrically determined couplings, accelerating scaling evolution, and a possible explanation for a small dynamical dark-energy density?

sources.title: Hybrid dark sector: Locked quintessence and dark matter

evidence.text: Can coupled supersymmetric flat-direction scalars account for dark matter and present dark energy, attain suitable initial conditions after inflation, and terminate accelerated expansion in the future?

sources.title: Emergent Dark Universe and the Swampland Criteria

evidence.text: The hEDU setting attributes the dark sector to extrinsic geometry rather than additional matter on the hypersurface. Ordinary matter sources a four-dimensional induced-gravity equation supplemented by a Brown–York boundary stress tensor.

sources.title: Draining the Swampland

evidence.text: Could a drainon also account for dark matter while a cosmological constant explains current acceleration?
